meta.title: AQA GCSE Mathematics (8300) question bank with self-check rubrics
meta.verification_note: Content reference IDs from the AQA specification. Marking conventions were sampled from AQA June 2023 8300/1F, 1H and 3H mark schemes only. Individual questions and accepted-answer lists have NOT been verified against every past paper; see review_status.

self_check_matching_spec.purpose: How an app should use criteria[].examples and the rule object on each criterion. Reference implementation: mengine.py (+ pengine.py for keyword rules).
student_flow: Student answers (typed, or photographed/typed working). App may pre-suggest ticks from the rules (mark source = auto_suggest).
Student ticks each criterion they believe they met (mark source = student_self). Model answer stays hidden until the attempt is submitted.
Store one attempt_criterion_checks row per criterion with student_says_met and model_answer_viewed_at; independent/teacher marking goes in separate columns.

mark_codes.M: method mark (correct method that could lead to a correct answer)
mark_codes.Mdep: method mark that depends on the previous method mark
mark_codes.A: accuracy mark (follows from a correct method; method may be implied)
mark_codes.SC: special case: partial credit for a common misinterpretation

self_check_matching_spec.implied_marks: A criterion with also_met_if_criterion_met = Cn is also awarded when Cn (the correct final answer) is met: AQA awards full marks for a correct answer without working unless the question says 'show' / 'you must show your working'.

numeric_rule.equivalences_accepted: decimal, fraction (any equivalent unless simplify_required), mixed number, improper fraction, percentage (35% = 0.35 and 35), standard form (7.2 x 10^-3, 7.2e-3, 7.2×10⁻³), money (£6.10, 6.10, 610p), thousands separators, trailing zeros
numeric_rule.reject_unprocessed_fraction: default true when expected_value is an integer: 270/6 does not earn the mark for 45
numeric_rule.no_decimal_fractions: default true: 18.75/10 does not count as a fraction
numeric_rule.simplify_required: fraction must be in lowest terms
numeric_rule.forms: optional whitelist of kinds: int, dec, frac, mixed, pct, sf
numeric_rule.alternative_answers: other equally acceptable values (e.g. 25 for a percentage)
numeric_rule.accepted_units / unit_required: unit_required is false for most maths questions ('ignore units' in AQA marking); when true a correct value with a wrong unit does not earn the mark

expression_rule.sample_points: list of {at:{var:value}, value:number}; the student's expression is parsed and evaluated at each point, so any algebraically equivalent form passes
expression_rule.form: simplified | expanded (no brackets, max_terms terms) | factorised (must contain brackets)
expression_rule.require_lhs: for equations such as y = 2x + 3 the left-hand side must be this letter
expression_rule.alternatives: other accepted equivalent targets (e.g. a partially expanded step)
expression_rule.parsing: implicit multiplication (2x, 3(x+1), (x+1)(x-2)), ^ or superscript powers, × * · for multiply, ÷ / for divide, √ and π

rule_types.inequality_rule: set of constraints on one variable; 13 > x equals x < 13; ≤ ⩽ <= all accepted; compound 1 ≤ a < 10 supported
rule_types.values_rule: expected_values (ordered true/false); ignores letters such as x = 3, y = -1; fractions parsed
rule_types.ratio_rule: expected_ratio; equivalent ratios accepted unless simplest_required
rule_types.prime_factor_rule: index form or repeated multiplication of primes; multiset must match exactly
rule_types.keyword_rules: word/phrase matching for reasons and definitions (case-insensitive; stems, plurals, number words, US/UK spellings, typos on words of 5+ letters; see all_of / none_of / or)

self_check_matching_spec.examples_field: Examples show the kind of answer/working that earns the mark. They are NOT an exhaustive whitelist; anything satisfying the rule (or honestly judged by the student to contain the idea) earns the mark.
self_check_matching_spec.reject_examples: typical answers that do NOT earn the mark (wrong value, unprocessed fraction).

specification_points.title: Order numbers and use inequality symbols

misconceptions.misconception: A longer decimal is always bigger.
misconceptions.feedback: Compare place values: 0.5 is greater than 0.45.

misconceptions.misconception: The symbol < points to the larger number.
misconceptions.feedback: The small end of the symbol points to the smaller number.

specification_points.title: Four operations, place value, financial terms

misconceptions.misconception: Subtracting a negative makes the number smaller.
misconceptions.feedback: Subtracting a negative is the same as adding.

misconceptions.misconception: Profit is selling price plus cost price.
misconceptions.feedback: Profit = selling price − cost price.

misconceptions.misconception: Work left to right ignoring BIDMAS.
misconceptions.feedback: Brackets, indices, then division/multiplication, then addition/subtraction.

misconceptions.misconception: The reciprocal of 4 is -4.
misconceptions.feedback: The reciprocal of 4 is 1/4.

misconceptions.misconception: 1 is a prime number.
misconceptions.feedback: Primes have exactly two factors; 1 has only one.

misconceptions.misconception: LCM and HCF are the same thing.
misconceptions.feedback: HCF is the largest common factor; LCM is the smallest common multiple.

misconceptions.misconception: List outcomes in any order without checking for repeats.
misconceptions.feedback: List systematically so none are missed or repeated.

misconceptions.misconception: Add the options instead of multiplying them.
misconceptions.feedback: Use the product rule: multiply the number of choices.

misconceptions.misconception: 3² means 3 × 2.
misconceptions.feedback: 3² means 3 × 3.

misconceptions.misconception: The square root of 36 is 18.
misconceptions.feedback: Square root undoes squaring: √36 = 6.

misconceptions.misconception: x⁻² is negative.
misconceptions.feedback: A negative index means a reciprocal, not a negative number.

misconceptions.misconception: x^(1/2) means halve x.
misconceptions.feedback: x^(1/2) is the square root of x.

specification_points.title: Exact calculation with fractions, π and surds

misconceptions.feedback: You cannot add surds with different numbers under the root.

misconceptions.misconception: Write π as 3.14 in exact answers.
misconceptions.feedback: Leave π as a symbol for an exact answer.

misconceptions.misconception: 12 × 10³ is in standard form.
misconceptions.feedback: A must satisfy 1 ≤ A < 10.

misconceptions.misconception: A negative power means a negative number.
misconceptions.feedback: A negative power means a small number.

misconceptions.misconception: 1/3 = 0.3 exactly.
misconceptions.feedback: 1/3 = 0.333... recurring.

misconceptions.misconception: 2:3 means 2/3 and 1/3.
misconceptions.feedback: 2:3 means 2/5 and 3/5.

misconceptions.misconception: Add the ratio parts but forget to divide the total.
misconceptions.feedback: Divide the total by the number of parts first.

misconceptions.misconception: 20% of a number is dividing by 20.
misconceptions.feedback: 20% = 20/100, so divide by 5 (or multiply by 0.2).

misconceptions.misconception: Increase by 15% means multiply by 0.15.
misconceptions.feedback: Multiply by 1.15.

misconceptions.misconception: 1 m² = 100 cm².
Multiply to convert from small units to big units.
misconceptions.feedback: Converting small to big units means dividing.

misconceptions.misconception: Round to the nearest whole number for every estimate.
misconceptions.feedback: Round to 1 significant figure.

misconceptions.misconception: An estimate must be exactly equal to the answer.
misconceptions.feedback: An estimate is an approximate answer.

misconceptions.misconception: Rounding 3.456 to 2 d.p. gives 3.45.
misconceptions.feedback: Look at the third decimal place: 3.46.

misconceptions.misconception: Error interval 4.5 ≤ x ≤ 5.5.
misconceptions.feedback: Use < for the upper bound: 4.5 ≤ x < 5.5.

misconceptions.misconception: Upper bound of 12 (nearest whole) is 12.4.
misconceptions.feedback: Upper bound is 12.5.

misconceptions.misconception: Use lower bounds for every part of a calculation.
misconceptions.feedback: For a/b use upper a and lower b to get the maximum.

misconceptions.misconception: 3y means 3 + y.
misconceptions.feedback: 3y means 3 × y.

misconceptions.misconception: a² means a × 2.
misconceptions.feedback: a² means a × a.

misconceptions.misconception: 3x² with x = 4 is 12².
misconceptions.feedback: Square first: 3 × 16 = 48.

misconceptions.misconception: -x² with x = 3 is 9.
An expression has an equals sign.
misconceptions.feedback: An expression has no equals sign.

misconceptions.misconception: A formula and an equation are the same.
misconceptions.feedback: A formula links quantities; an equation is solved for an unknown.

misconceptions.misconception: Partly factorised answers are fully factorised.
misconceptions.feedback: Take out the highest common factor.

misconceptions.misconception: Move a term across the equals sign without changing its sign.
misconceptions.feedback: Use the inverse operation on both sides.

misconceptions.misconception: Rearrange P = 2l + 2w to l = P − 2w.
Checking with one example proves a statement.
misconceptions.feedback: A proof must work for all values.

misconceptions.misconception: An identity is solved to find x.
misconceptions.feedback: An identity is true for all values of x.

misconceptions.misconception: f(g(x)) means do f first.
misconceptions.feedback: Do g first, then f.

misconceptions.misconception: f⁻¹(x) is 1/f(x).
misconceptions.feedback: f⁻¹ is the inverse function, not the reciprocal.

misconceptions.misconception: Plot (3, −2) by going up 2.
misconceptions.feedback: The second value is the y-coordinate: down 2.

misconceptions.misconception: Write the y-coordinate first.
misconceptions.feedback: Coordinates are (x, y).

misconceptions.misconception: In y = mx + c, c is the gradient.
misconceptions.feedback: m is the gradient; c is the y-intercept.

misconceptions.misconception: Perpendicular lines have the same gradient.
misconceptions.feedback: Parallel lines share a gradient; perpendicular gradients multiply to −1.

misconceptions.misconception: Gradient = change in x ÷ change in y.
misconceptions.feedback: Gradient = change in y ÷ change in x.

misconceptions.misconception: The intercept is where the line crosses the x-axis.
misconceptions.feedback: The y-intercept is where x = 0.

misconceptions.misconception: The turning point is where the graph crosses the x-axis.
misconceptions.feedback: The turning point is the minimum or maximum point.

misconceptions.misconception: Roots are y-values.
misconceptions.feedback: Roots are x-values where y = 0.

misconceptions.misconception: y = x³ is a parabola.
misconceptions.feedback: y = x³ is a cubic graph.

misconceptions.misconception: A reciprocal graph touches the axes.
misconceptions.feedback: It approaches the axes but never touches them.

misconceptions.misconception: y = f(x) + 2 moves the graph left.
misconceptions.feedback: It moves up by 2.

misconceptions.misconception: y = f(x + 2) moves the graph right.
misconceptions.feedback: It moves left by 2.

misconceptions.misconception: A flat section on a distance-time graph means constant speed.
misconceptions.feedback: It means stationary.

misconceptions.misconception: Read values from the wrong axis.
misconceptions.feedback: Check which axis shows which quantity.

misconceptions.misconception: Area under a velocity-time graph is acceleration.
misconceptions.feedback: It is distance travelled; gradient is acceleration.

misconceptions.misconception: Gradient of a distance-time graph is distance.
misconceptions.feedback: It is speed.

misconceptions.misconception: x² + y² = r gives the radius r.
misconceptions.feedback: x² + y² = r², so the radius is the square root of the constant.

misconceptions.misconception: The tangent has the same gradient as the radius.
misconceptions.feedback: The tangent is perpendicular to the radius.

misconceptions.misconception: Add to both sides but subtract on one side only.
misconceptions.feedback: Do the same operation to both sides.

misconceptions.misconception: Forget to multiply every term in a bracket.
misconceptions.feedback: Expand the bracket fully first.

misconceptions.misconception: If (x − 2)(x − 3) = 0 then x = −2 and −3.
misconceptions.feedback: Each bracket equals zero: x = 2 and x = 3.

misconceptions.misconception: Solve x² = 25 as x = 5 only.
misconceptions.feedback: There are two solutions: ±5.

misconceptions.misconception: Finding x is enough.
misconceptions.feedback: Find both x and y, then check in both equations.

misconceptions.misconception: Subtract when signs differ.
misconceptions.feedback: If the signs differ, add the equations to eliminate.

misconceptions.misconception: Round at every step of an iteration.
misconceptions.feedback: Keep full calculator accuracy and round only the final answer.

misconceptions.misconception: The answer is the last value you wrote.
misconceptions.feedback: The answer is the value the iterations converge to.

misconceptions.misconception: Translate 'five more than n' as 5n.
misconceptions.feedback: It is n + 5.

misconceptions.misconception: Perimeter is the same as area.
misconceptions.feedback: Perimeter adds the sides; area multiplies lengths.

misconceptions.misconception: An open circle means the end value is included.
misconceptions.feedback: A closed circle means included; an open circle means not included.

misconceptions.misconception: Dividing by a negative keeps the sign direction.
misconceptions.feedback: Reverse the inequality sign.

misconceptions.misconception: The 10th term of 3n + 1 is 3 + 10.
misconceptions.feedback: Substitute n = 10: 3 × 10 + 1 = 31.

misconceptions.misconception: The term-to-term rule and nth term are the same.
misconceptions.feedback: Term-to-term needs the previous term; nth term gives the term from its position.

misconceptions.misconception: Triangular numbers are 3, 6, 9.
misconceptions.feedback: Triangular numbers are 1, 3, 6, 10, 15.

misconceptions.misconception: A geometric sequence adds the same number.
misconceptions.feedback: A geometric sequence multiplies by a constant ratio.

misconceptions.misconception: nth term of 5, 8, 11 is n + 3.
misconceptions.feedback: The common difference is 3, so 3n + 2.

misconceptions.misconception: The nth term of a quadratic sequence is linear.
misconceptions.feedback: Quadratic sequences have an n² term.

misconceptions.misconception: 1 hour = 100 minutes.
misconceptions.feedback: 1 hour = 60 minutes.

misconceptions.misconception: Convert speed units by converting only the distance.
misconceptions.feedback: Convert the time units too.

specification_points.title: Scale factors, scale diagrams and maps

misconceptions.misconception: Divide when enlarging.
misconceptions.feedback: Multiply by the scale factor to enlarge.

misconceptions.misconception: Scale 1 : 50 000 means 1 cm is 50 cm.
misconceptions.feedback: 1 cm represents 50 000 cm = 500 m.

specification_points.title: Expressing one quantity as a fraction of another

misconceptions.misconception: 12 out of 20 is 12/8.
Put the larger number on the bottom always.
misconceptions.feedback: The 'whole' goes on the bottom, even if it is smaller.

misconceptions.misconception: 8 : 12 is in simplest form.
misconceptions.feedback: Divide both parts by 4 to get 2 : 3.

misconceptions.misconception: Mixed units can be compared directly.
misconceptions.feedback: Convert to the same units first.

misconceptions.misconception: Divide the total by each ratio number separately.
misconceptions.feedback: Divide the total by the sum of the parts.

misconceptions.misconception: A ratio of 2 : 3 splits the total into 2 and 3.
misconceptions.feedback: It splits into 2/5 and 3/5 of the total.

misconceptions.misconception: 'A is 3 times B' means B is 3 times A.
misconceptions.feedback: If A = 3B then B = A/3.

misconceptions.misconception: Compare quantities by difference only.
misconceptions.feedback: Multiplicative comparison uses ratios.

misconceptions.misconception: Doubling the people means doubling the cooking time.
misconceptions.feedback: Ingredient amounts scale; cooking time does not.

misconceptions.misconception: Use addition to scale a recipe.
misconceptions.feedback: Multiply every quantity by the same factor.

misconceptions.misconception: y : x = 2 : 3 means y = 3x/2.
misconceptions.feedback: y : x = 2 : 3 means y = 2x/3.

misconceptions.misconception: The ratio 1 : 4 means a fraction of 1/4.
misconceptions.feedback: 1 : 4 means 1/5 and 4/5 of the whole.

misconceptions.misconception: A 20% increase then 20% decrease returns to the start.
misconceptions.feedback: The decrease is of the larger number, so you end lower.

misconceptions.misconception: Percentage change = change ÷ new value.
misconceptions.feedback: Divide by the original value.

misconceptions.misconception: Inverse proportion means one goes up as the other goes down by the same amount.
misconceptions.feedback: Inverse proportion keeps the product constant.

misconceptions.misconception: Direct proportion graph can have a y-intercept.
misconceptions.feedback: A direct proportion graph is a straight line through the origin.

misconceptions.misconception: Speed = time ÷ distance.
misconceptions.feedback: Speed = distance ÷ time.

misconceptions.misconception: Density = volume ÷ mass.
misconceptions.feedback: Density = mass ÷ volume.

specification_points.title: Comparing lengths, areas and volumes using ratio

misconceptions.misconception: If lengths double, area doubles.
misconceptions.feedback: Area scale factor is k²; volume is k³.

misconceptions.misconception: Use the length scale factor for volumes.
misconceptions.feedback: Cube the length scale factor.

misconceptions.misconception: y inversely proportional to x is y = kx.
misconceptions.feedback: It is y = k/x.

misconceptions.misconception: y ∝ x² means y = 2x.
misconceptions.feedback: y ∝ x² means y = kx².

specification_points.title: Gradient as a rate of change

misconceptions.misconception: The gradient of a distance-time graph is distance.
misconceptions.feedback: It is speed (rate of change of distance).

misconceptions.misconception: Rate of change is the y-intercept.
misconceptions.feedback: Rate of change is the gradient.

specification_points.title: Instantaneous and average rate of change

misconceptions.misconception: Gradient of a chord gives the rate at a point.
misconceptions.feedback: A chord gives an average rate; a tangent gives the instantaneous rate.

misconceptions.misconception: Draw the tangent through any two points of the curve.
misconceptions.feedback: A tangent touches the curve at one point.

misconceptions.misconception: Compound interest is the same as simple interest.
misconceptions.feedback: Compound interest is calculated on the new total each period.

misconceptions.misconception: 5% growth for 3 years is 15%.
misconceptions.feedback: Multiply by 1.05 three times: 1.05³.

misconceptions.misconception: A rhombus has four right angles.
misconceptions.feedback: A rhombus has equal sides; a square has right angles.

misconceptions.misconception: Parallel lines can meet.
misconceptions.feedback: Parallel lines are always the same distance apart.

misconceptions.misconception: A perpendicular bisector is any line through the midpoint.
misconceptions.feedback: It is perpendicular and passes through the midpoint.

misconceptions.misconception: Use any compass width for every arc.
misconceptions.feedback: Keep the compass width the same for the construction.

misconceptions.misconception: Angles on a straight line sum to 360°.
misconceptions.feedback: They sum to 180°.

misconceptions.misconception: Alternate angles are on the same side of the transversal.
misconceptions.feedback: Alternate angles are on opposite sides of the transversal and between the parallel lines (they make a Z shape). Use the term 'alternate' in your reason.

misconceptions.misconception: A square is not a rectangle.
misconceptions.feedback: A square is a special rectangle.

misconceptions.misconception: A trapezium has two pairs of parallel sides.
misconceptions.feedback: A trapezium has exactly one pair.

misconceptions.misconception: AAA proves triangles congruent.
misconceptions.feedback: AAA only shows similarity; congruence needs SSS, SAS, ASA or RHS.

misconceptions.misconception: Congruent shapes can differ in size.
misconceptions.feedback: Congruent shapes are identical in shape and size.

specification_points.title: Proof using angle facts and congruence

misconceptions.misconception: Measure the angles to prove a result.
misconceptions.feedback: A proof uses known facts and reasons.

misconceptions.misconception: Base angles of an isosceles triangle are unequal.
misconceptions.feedback: Base angles of an isosceles triangle are equal.

misconceptions.misconception: A reflection moves the shape along.
misconceptions.feedback: A reflection flips across a mirror line.

misconceptions.misconception: An enlargement only needs a scale factor.
misconceptions.feedback: Give the scale factor and the centre.

specification_points.title: Combined transformations and vectors for translation

misconceptions.misconception: The vector (3, −2) means 3 down and 2 right.
misconceptions.feedback: Top number is x (right), bottom is y: 3 right, 2 down.

misconceptions.misconception: Order of transformations never matters.
misconceptions.feedback: The order can change the result.

misconceptions.misconception: The diameter is half the radius.
misconceptions.feedback: The diameter is twice the radius.

misconceptions.misconception: A chord must go through the centre.
misconceptions.feedback: A chord joins two points on the circle; the diameter is the longest chord.

misconceptions.misconception: Angle in a semicircle is 180°.
misconceptions.feedback: It is 90°.

misconceptions.misconception: Opposite angles in a cyclic quadrilateral are equal.
misconceptions.feedback: They sum to 180°.

misconceptions.misconception: The midpoint is the difference of the coordinates.
misconceptions.feedback: Add the coordinates and halve.

misconceptions.misconception: Distance between points is x difference plus y difference.
misconceptions.feedback: Use Pythagoras on the differences.

misconceptions.misconception: A cube has 6 vertices.
misconceptions.feedback: A cube has 8 vertices, 12 edges, 6 faces.

misconceptions.misconception: A cone has two flat faces.
misconceptions.feedback: A cone has one flat face and one curved surface.

misconceptions.misconception: The plan is the view from the front.
misconceptions.feedback: The plan is the view from above.

misconceptions.misconception: Hidden edges are always drawn solid.
misconceptions.feedback: Hidden edges are shown dashed in some conventions or omitted.

misconceptions.misconception: 1 litre = 100 ml.
misconceptions.feedback: 1 litre = 1000 ml.

misconceptions.misconception: 1 m³ = 100 litres.
misconceptions.feedback: 1 m³ = 1000 litres.

misconceptions.misconception: Bearings are measured anticlockwise.
misconceptions.feedback: Bearings are measured clockwise from north.

misconceptions.misconception: Bearings can be two digits.
misconceptions.feedback: Write three figures: 070°.

misconceptions.misconception: Area of triangle is base × height.
misconceptions.feedback: Area of triangle is ½ × base × height.

misconceptions.misconception: Volume of a prism is the perimeter times length.
misconceptions.feedback: Volume of a prism = cross-section area × length.

misconceptions.misconception: Circumference = πr².
misconceptions.feedback: Circumference = 2πr or πd; area = πr².

misconceptions.misconception: Use the diameter in πr².
misconceptions.feedback: Halve the diameter to get r.

misconceptions.misconception: Arc length = angle/360 × πr².
misconceptions.feedback: Arc length = angle/360 × 2πr.

misconceptions.misconception: Sector area = angle/360 × 2πr.
misconceptions.feedback: Sector area = angle/360 × πr².

misconceptions.misconception: The area scale factor equals the length scale factor.
misconceptions.feedback: Area scale factor = (length scale factor)².

misconceptions.misconception: Similar shapes have equal lengths.
misconceptions.feedback: Similar shapes have equal angles and proportional lengths.

misconceptions.misconception: Pythagoras: a + b = c.
misconceptions.feedback: a² + b² = c².

misconceptions.misconception: Use sin for adjacent and hypotenuse.
misconceptions.feedback: cos = adjacent/hypotenuse; sin = opposite/hypotenuse.

misconceptions.misconception: Use the sine rule for any pair of sides.
misconceptions.feedback: Use it with an angle opposite a side.

misconceptions.misconception: Cosine rule with the wrong sign.
misconceptions.feedback: a² = b² + c² − 2bc cos A.

specification_points.title: Area of a triangle using sin C

misconceptions.misconception: Use any angle in ½ab sin C.
misconceptions.feedback: C is the angle between sides a and b.

misconceptions.misconception: Forget the ½.
misconceptions.feedback: Area = ½ab sin C.

misconceptions.misconception: A vector has no direction.
misconceptions.feedback: A vector has magnitude and direction.

misconceptions.misconception: Reverse a vector by swapping numbers.
misconceptions.feedback: Reverse by changing both signs.

misconceptions.misconception: AB = A − B.
misconceptions.feedback: AB = b − a (end minus start).

misconceptions.misconception: Parallel vectors must be equal.
misconceptions.feedback: Parallel vectors are multiples of each other.

misconceptions.misconception: Relative frequency is the same as the theoretical probability.
misconceptions.feedback: Relative frequency comes from an experiment and approximates the theory.

misconceptions.misconception: Write probability as a ratio.
misconceptions.feedback: Use a fraction, decimal or percentage.

misconceptions.misconception: Probability 1/6 means exactly 1 in every 6 rolls.
misconceptions.feedback: It is an expected proportion over many trials.

misconceptions.misconception: Expected number = probability + trials.
misconceptions.feedback: Expected number = probability × number of trials.

misconceptions.misconception: Probability can be greater than 1.
misconceptions.feedback: Probabilities lie between 0 and 1.

misconceptions.misconception: 'Unlikely' means impossible.
misconceptions.feedback: Unlikely means a low probability, not zero.

misconceptions.misconception: Add probabilities of non-exhaustive outcomes to get 1.
misconceptions.feedback: Only an exhaustive set of mutually exclusive outcomes sums to 1.

misconceptions.misconception: P(not A) = P(A) − 1.
misconceptions.feedback: P(not A) = 1 − P(A).

misconceptions.misconception: A bigger sample guarantees the theoretical value.
misconceptions.feedback: Larger samples tend towards it.

misconceptions.misconception: Few trials give reliable results.
misconceptions.feedback: More trials give more reliable results.

misconceptions.misconception: Count the overlap twice.
misconceptions.feedback: Count the intersection once.

misconceptions.misconception: Union means 'and'.
misconceptions.feedback: Union is 'or'; intersection is 'and'.

misconceptions.misconception: Outcomes of two dice are 6 + 6 = 12.
misconceptions.feedback: There are 6 × 6 = 36 outcomes.

misconceptions.misconception: All sums are equally likely.
misconceptions.feedback: Sums have different numbers of ways.

misconceptions.misconception: Always add probabilities.
misconceptions.feedback: Multiply for 'and'; add for 'or' (mutually exclusive).

misconceptions.misconception: Without replacement keep the same probabilities.
misconceptions.feedback: The denominator reduces without replacement.

misconceptions.misconception: P(A given B) = P(A and B).
misconceptions.feedback: Divide by P(B): P(A|B) = P(A and B)/P(B).

misconceptions.misconception: Use the original total instead of the restricted total.
misconceptions.feedback: The sample space is reduced to B.

misconceptions.misconception: A bigger sample is always unbiased.
misconceptions.feedback: A sample must also be representative and random.

misconceptions.misconception: Asking friends is a random sample.
misconceptions.feedback: Random sampling gives every member an equal chance.

misconceptions.misconception: The pie chart angle is the frequency.
misconceptions.feedback: Angle = frequency/total × 360.

misconceptions.misconception: Bar chart bars should touch.
misconceptions.feedback: Bars for categorical data have gaps; histogram bars touch.

misconceptions.misconception: Height of a histogram bar is frequency.
misconceptions.feedback: Height is frequency density = frequency ÷ class width.

misconceptions.misconception: Plot cumulative frequency at the class midpoint.
misconceptions.feedback: Plot at the upper class boundary.

misconceptions.misconception: The mean is the middle value.
misconceptions.feedback: The median is the middle value; the mean is the total ÷ number of values.
